tasks.title: Retain first occurrences throughout a list
tasks.description: ListWeave is a small in-memory library for arranging JSON list data. This snapshot contains unique(values). A duplicate-filtering refactor now misses repeats separated by other entries. Restore the documented contract. values is either a JSON list or None; other argument types are outside this task contract. All JSON numbers are finite and integers stay within the JavaScript safe range.

requirements.text: For a list values, unique returns the first member of each Python == equality class, in original first-occurrence order. Equality is recursive for lists and dictionaries; strings compare exactly without Unicode normalization, and Python numeric equality includes True == 1 and False == 0. Nested JSON values and None elements are supported. The empty list returns [].
For list input, unique leaves the caller list and all its nested lists and dictionaries unchanged, including when removing nonadjacent duplicates.
Passing None as values raises TypeError.

tasks.title: Preserve a final partial list block
tasks.description: This ListWeave snapshot exposes blocks(values, width), used to divide in-memory list data into consecutive display batches. A loop-bound regression drops a final short batch. Restore all documented behaviors. All inputs and outputs are JSON values; numbers are finite and integers are within JavaScript safe range.

requirements.text: For list values and a positive integer width, blocks returns consecutive nonempty sublists of at most width elements in original order. Every element appears exactly once. Include the final short block without padding; width 1 produces singleton blocks, and an empty values returns [].
For valid calls, blocks leaves values and its nested lists and dictionaries unchanged, including calls with a final partial block.

values must be a list and width must have Python type int, excluding booleans; any violation raises TypeError. With those types valid, zero or negative width raises ValueError, including when values is empty.

tasks.title: Honor signed cyclic list shifts
tasks.description: This ListWeave snapshot contains rotate(values, steps), an in-memory sequence reordering helper. A refactor that handles the shift magnitude lost the leftward direction of negative steps. Restore the documented signed rotation. Inputs and outputs are JSON values with finite numbers and JavaScript-safe integers.

requirements.text: For list values and integer steps, rotate moves elements cyclically right by steps positions when positive and left by -steps when negative, preserving relative cyclic order. Reduce steps modulo list length; zero and whole-length multiples keep the order, a singleton keeps its value, and an empty list returns [] for every integer steps.
For valid calls, rotate leaves values and all nested lists and dictionaries unchanged, including negative shifts that change the returned order.
values must be a list and steps must have Python type int, excluding booleans; any violation raises TypeError, even when values is empty.

tasks.title: Keep unpaired values during list weaving
tasks.description: This ListWeave snapshot provides interleave(left, right), which weaves two in-memory sequences for a paired display. A zip-based refactor loses entries when list lengths differ. Restore the full documented behavior for JSON data; numbers are finite and integers stay within JavaScript safe range.

requirements.text: For lists left and right, interleave returns left[0], right[0], left[1], right[1], and so on while both have elements, then all remaining elements of the longer list in their original order. Empty lists are supported, including both empty. Every occurrence is retained, even equal or nested JSON values.
For valid calls, interleave leaves both caller lists and all nested lists and dictionaries unchanged, including unequal-length inputs.
Both left and right must be lists; if either is any other JSON type, including None, raise TypeError before producing a result.

tasks.title: Count adjacent list runs independently
tasks.description: This ListWeave snapshot contains runs(values), a compact representation of consecutive repeated list items for in-memory display summaries. A counting refactor merged separate runs of the same value. Restore the adjacent-run contract for JSON data, with finite numbers and JavaScript-safe integers.

requirements.text: For list values, runs returns one {"value": first_item, "count": positive_integer} object for each maximal contiguous Python == run, in order. Nonadjacent equal values stay separate. Equality is recursive for lists and dictionaries, exact for strings without Unicode normalization, and includes Python numeric equality True == 1 and False == 0. Each run retains its first item as value; None and empty nested containers are supported. Empty input returns [].
For list input, runs leaves the caller list and all nested lists and dictionaries unchanged, including repeated values in separate runs.
A non-list values of any JSON type, including None, raises TypeError.

tasks.title: Repeated page marks fragment contiguous reading runs
tasks.description: The reading log receives repeated page marks after manual imports. Repair page_runs(pages) while retaining its inclusive, sorted run representation and validation behavior.

requirements.text: page_runs(pages) returns sorted inclusive [first,last] pairs covering exactly the distinct input page numbers. Consecutive integers belong to one run; gaps start new runs. Input order and duplicate occurrences do not affect the result. An empty list returns [].
The function must leave the supplied pages list unchanged, including element order and duplicate occurrences, on both successful returns and ValueError paths.

pages must be a list whose every element is a plain integer from 1 through 1000000 inclusive. Booleans, floats, strings (including Unicode), null, out-of-range integers and non-list outer values are invalid; raise ValueError for any invalid input.

tasks.title: Exact-capacity sessions split too early
tasks.description: Whole-chapter sessions unexpectedly split when their combined page count equals the configured limit. Repair chapter_sessions(chapter_lengths, limit) without changing input order or the handling of oversized chapters.

requirements.text: chapter_sessions(chapter_lengths, limit) returns lists of whole chapter lengths in original order, greedily filling each session while its sum stays <= limit. Flush a nonempty session before a chapter that would make its sum exceed limit. An individually oversized chapter must occupy its own session unchanged. Never emit empty sessions; empty input returns [].
The chapter_lengths list must remain unchanged on successful returns and ValueError paths, including when multiple chapters fit exactly into a session or a chapter is oversized.

chapter_lengths must be a list of plain integers from 1 through 1000000 inclusive, and limit must be a plain integer in the same range. Reject booleans, floats, strings (including Unicode), null, out-of-range integers and a non-list chapter_lengths value with ValueError.

tasks.title: Chapter boundary pages resolve to the wrong chapter
tasks.description: The reading position view has an off-by-one error at chapter endings. Repair locate_page(chapter_lengths, page), retaining one-based indices and the positions of zero-length chapters in chapter numbering.

requirements.text: locate_page(chapter_lengths, page) returns {"chapter": c, "page": p} for the chapter containing the one-based book page, with both c and p one-based. A chapter includes its last page. Zero-length chapters consume no book pages but retain their positions in chapter numbering. Return null when the book page exceeds the total length, including for empty/all-zero chapter lists.
The chapter_lengths list must be unchanged after a successful return or ValueError, preserving zero-length entries and their order.

chapter_lengths must be a list of plain integers from 0 through 1000000 inclusive; page must be a plain integer from 1 through 1000000 inclusive. Booleans, floats, strings (including Unicode), null, out-of-range values and a non-list chapter_lengths value must raise ValueError.

tasks.title: Later reading sessions replace earlier page totals
tasks.description: The book-club summary currently loses earlier sessions for a title. Repair reading_totals(records) while preserving exact title identity and the order in which titles first appear.

requirements.text: reading_totals(records) returns one {"book": title, "pages": sum} record for each distinct exact book string, ordered by first occurrence. Sum all page counts for that string. Title matching is case-sensitive and performs no trimming or Unicode normalization. Empty strings and zero totals remain represented. Empty input returns [].
The supplied records list and every record dictionary must remain unchanged on successful returns and ValueError paths, including duplicate-title aggregation.

records must be a list of dictionaries with exactly the keys "book" and "pages". book must be a string, with any Unicode content including an empty string allowed. pages must be a plain integer from 0 through 1000000 inclusive. Any invalid outer value, entry, key set, title type or page value (including booleans, floats and null) raises ValueError.

tasks.title: Half-percent progress ties round down unexpectedly
tasks.description: The progress badge uses the wrong rounding rule at exact half-percent values. Repair reading_percentage(completed, total) while retaining saturation and strict count validation.

requirements.text: For valid counts with completed < total, reading_percentage(completed, total) returns the nearest integer to 100 * completed / total, rounding an exact halfway value upward. In particular, zero completed pages returns 0. The result is a JSON integer.
For valid counts with completed >= total, return exactly 100, including counts beyond the planned total.

completed must be a plain integer from 0 through 1000000 inclusive, and total must be a plain integer from 1 through 1000000 inclusive. Reject booleans, floats, strings (including Unicode), null and any out-of-range value with ValueError.

tasks.title: Retain fill-down history across blank worksheet spans
tasks.description: Gridloom is an original stdlib-only worksheet library. This task concerns the named operation; retain all other functions. Inputs and outputs are JSON values. A valid worksheet is a list of lists whose cells are None or exact integers (booleans and floats are not integers). Integer inputs and all aggregate sums in scope are within the JavaScript safe range. No function may mutate any caller argument, including before raising an error. Empty rows and an empty worksheet are supported. Repair the reported regression while preserving the full contract below. The current fill-down refactor forgets earlier column values after blank spans.

requirements.text: fill_down(rows) replaces each explicit None cell with the most recent integer in the same column in any earlier input row, or leaves it None if no earlier integer exists. Explicit integers, including zero and negatives, remain unchanged. Carrying through consecutive None cells must keep the last integer.

Preserve the number and order of rows and the exact length of every row. Missing columns and empty rows do not clear earlier column history and do not gain new cells. An empty worksheet returns [], and empty rows remain [].

Reject a non-list worksheet, any non-list row, or any cell other than None or an exact integer with TypeError; this includes rejecting booleans, floats, strings (including Unicode), lists and objects as cells. Validate all rows, including rows after otherwise valid data.

tasks.title: Keep explicit empty cells during worksheet transposition
tasks.description: Gridloom is an original stdlib-only worksheet library. This task concerns the named operation; retain all other functions. Inputs and outputs are JSON values. A valid worksheet is a list of lists whose cells are None or exact integers (booleans and floats are not integers). Integer inputs and all aggregate sums in scope are within the JavaScript safe range. No function may mutate any caller argument, including before raising an error. Empty rows and an empty worksheet are supported. Repair the reported regression while preserving the full contract below. The current transpose helper treats explicit None cells as padding.

requirements.text: For transpose(rows, fill=0), every existing input cell at row r and column c must appear unchanged at output row c and column r, including explicit None, zero and negative integers. Preserve both coordinate orders.

The result has max input-row length rows (zero when there are no cells), each with len(rows) cells. Use fill only where the corresponding input row lacks that column. The default fill is 0; None is a permitted fill. Empty input or only empty rows returns [].

Reject a non-list worksheet, any non-list row, or any cell other than None or an exact integer with TypeError; this includes rejecting booleans, floats, strings (including Unicode), lists and objects as cells. Validate all rows, including rows after otherwise valid data. Also reject fill unless it is None or an exact integer, even when the worksheet is empty.

tasks.title: Include the final complete worksheet window
tasks.description: Gridloom is an original stdlib-only worksheet library. This task concerns the named operation; retain all other functions. Inputs and outputs are JSON values. A valid worksheet is a list of lists whose cells are None or exact integers (booleans and floats are not integers). Integer inputs and all aggregate sums in scope are within the JavaScript safe range. No function may mutate any caller argument, including before raising an error. Empty rows and an empty worksheet are supported. Repair the reported regression while preserving the full contract below. The complete-window boundary check drops the last band when it ends exactly at the worksheet boundary.

requirements.text: row_windows(rows, size, stride=1) returns each complete consecutive window of exactly size rows starting at indices 0, stride, 2*stride, and so on. Include a complete window ending exactly at len(rows). Preserve window order and each row and cell within it, including empty rows and None cells; overlapping windows are allowed.
Omit every incomplete trailing window. If rows is empty or size exceeds len(rows), return []. A stride larger than size may leave gaps and must not manufacture intermediate windows or a partial tail.

Reject a non-list worksheet, any non-list row, or any cell other than None or an exact integer with TypeError; this includes rejecting booleans, floats, strings (including Unicode), lists and objects as cells. Validate all rows, including rows after otherwise valid data. Require size and stride to be exact integers (not bool or float), otherwise TypeError. After type validation, either value <= 0 raises ValueError.

tasks.title: Count zero-valued worksheet cells as populated
tasks.description: Gridloom is an original stdlib-only worksheet library. This task concerns the named operation; retain all other functions. Inputs and outputs are JSON values. A valid worksheet is a list of lists whose cells are None or exact integers (booleans and floats are not integers). Integer inputs and all aggregate sums in scope are within the JavaScript safe range. No function may mutate any caller argument, including before raising an error. Empty rows and an empty worksheet are supported. Repair the reported regression while preserving the full contract below. A truthiness shortcut undercounts columns containing explicit zero cells.

requirements.text: column_summary(rows) returns one {"sum": integer, "count": integer} object per column, ordered from column zero through the longest row. sum is the signed integer sum of all present non-None cells in that column; missing cells and None contribute zero. A column with no integers has sum 0. Empty input or only empty rows returns [].

For each returned column, count is the number of present non-None cells in that column. Explicit zero and negative integers each count as one; missing cells and explicit None count as zero. A column with no integers has count 0.

Reject a non-list worksheet, any non-list row, or any cell other than None or an exact integer with TypeError; this includes rejecting booleans, floats, strings (including Unicode), lists and objects as cells. Validate all rows, including rows after otherwise valid data.

tasks.title: Limit worksheet row deduplication to consecutive runs
tasks.description: Gridloom is an original stdlib-only worksheet library. This task concerns the named operation; retain all other functions. Inputs and outputs are JSON values. A valid worksheet is a list of lists whose cells are None or exact integers (booleans and floats are not integers). Integer inputs and all aggregate sums in scope are within the JavaScript safe range. No function may mutate any caller argument, including before raising an error. Empty rows and an empty worksheet are supported. Repair the reported regression while preserving the full contract below. The current deduplication optimization removes later runs that happen to match earlier rows.

requirements.text: collapse_rows(rows) keeps exactly one representative row from each maximal consecutive run of equal rows. Rows are equal only when they have the same length and corresponding cells are equal, with None distinct from every integer. Preserve all cell positions and values; different rows must not collapse merely because their length or sum matches.

Preserve the order of runs and retain a row when an unequal row separates it from an earlier equal row, including separated empty rows or None-containing rows. Only neighboring equal rows collapse. An empty worksheet returns [].

Reject a non-list worksheet, any non-list row, or any cell other than None or an exact integer with TypeError; this includes rejecting booleans, floats, strings (including Unicode), lists and objects as cells. Validate all rows, including rows after otherwise valid data.

tasks.title: Restore adjacency-aware band coalescing
tasks.description: RibbonPlan stores a ribbon as an ordered list of colored bands. A recent aggregation refactor changed coalesce so separated occurrences of a color lose their positions. Restore the retained ordered-band contract.

requirements.text: coalesce(bands) returns a list of color/length records obtained by replacing each maximal consecutive run of exactly equal color strings with one record whose length is their sum. Preserve run order and label text. Equal colors separated by another color remain separate. An empty input returns [].

bands must be a list of at most 1000 dictionaries, each with exactly color and length keys. color must be a nonempty string; Unicode, case and spaces are literal label content. length must be an integer from 1 through 1000000, excluding booleans. Invalid bands, records, keys or field values raise ValueError, including None, an empty color, and noninteger lengths.

The function must leave the caller's bands list and every contained record unchanged, both on a successful return and when raising ValueError. This includes ordinary nonempty calls whose result differs from the input.

tasks.title: Restore partial-band span extraction
tasks.description: RibbonPlan extracts material spans using integer positions measured from the start of the ribbon. An optimization stopped including partial bands at span edges. Restore the established half-open extraction behavior.

requirements.text: slice_span(bands, start, stop) returns the portion in the half-open interval [start, stop), using cumulative band lengths as coordinates. Emit each positive overlap in original order with its color and overlap length. Retain original band boundaries even for neighboring equal colors. Clip positions beyond the total length. Empty input, start == stop, or start at or beyond the total returns [].

bands must be a list of at most 1000 dictionaries, each with exactly color and length keys. color must be a nonempty string; Unicode, case and spaces are literal label content. length must be an integer from 1 through 1000000, excluding booleans. Invalid bands, records, keys or field values raise ValueError, including None, an empty color, and noninteger lengths. start and stop must be integers excluding booleans, each from 0 through 1000000000, with start <= stop; otherwise raise ValueError.

The function must leave the caller's bands list and every contained record unchanged, both on a successful return and when raising ValueError. This includes ordinary nonempty calls whose result differs from the input.

tasks.title: Restore whole-pattern tile order
tasks.description: RibbonPlan tiles a short ribbon pattern for assembly planning. A loop refactor now repeats each band separately and changes the pattern order. Restore whole-pattern repetition and its retained boundaries.

requirements.text: tile(bands, count) returns count consecutive copies of the complete band sequence, in that order, with each output record containing the original color and length. Preserve every original band boundary and every boundary between copies, including neighboring equal colors; do not multiply lengths or coalesce bands. count == 0 or empty bands returns [].

bands must be a list of at most 1000 dictionaries, each with exactly color and length keys. color must be a nonempty string; Unicode, case and spaces are literal label content. length must be an integer from 1 through 1000000, excluding booleans. Invalid bands, records, keys or field values raise ValueError, including None, an empty color, and noninteger lengths. count must be an integer from 0 through 1000, excluding booleans; otherwise raise ValueError. Validate bands even when count is zero.

The function must leave the caller's bands list and every contained record unchanged, both on a successful return and when raising ValueError. This includes ordinary nonempty calls whose result differs from the input.

tasks.title: Restore first-use order in material totals
tasks.description: RibbonPlan summarizes material quantities in the order colors first appear on a pattern. A presentation refactor sorts the totals by color and disrupts that retained order. Restore the summary contract.

requirements.text: color_totals(bands) returns one color/length record for every distinct exact color string, ordered by that color's first appearance in bands. length is the sum of all input lengths for that color, including separated occurrences. Preserve label text; case variants and differently spaced strings remain distinct. Empty input returns [].

bands must be a list of at most 1000 dictionaries, each with exactly color and length keys. color must be a nonempty string; Unicode, case and spaces are literal label content. length must be an integer from 1 through 1000000, excluding booleans. Invalid bands, records, keys or field values raise ValueError, including None, an empty color, and noninteger lengths.

The function must leave the caller's bands list and every contained record unchanged, both on a successful return and when raising ValueError. This includes ordinary nonempty calls whose result differs from the input.

tasks.title: Restore material-distance ribbon rotation
tasks.description: RibbonPlan rotates a pattern so a chosen material position becomes its new start. A simplification interpreted the offset as a band count. Restore the distance-based rotation used by layout planning.

requirements.text: rotate(bands, offset) rotates left by offset material units modulo the sum of band lengths; negative offsets therefore rotate right. Cut within a band when needed: output its remaining suffix, subsequent bands, preceding bands, then its positive prefix. Preserve every preexisting boundary and the new cut boundary; never coalesce equal colors. A cut exactly at a boundary produces no zero-length record. Zero or a multiple of total length retains the sequence. Empty input returns [].

bands must be a list of at most 1000 dictionaries, each with exactly color and length keys. color must be a nonempty string; Unicode, case and spaces are literal label content. length must be an integer from 1 through 1000000, excluding booleans. Invalid bands, records, keys or field values raise ValueError, including None, an empty color, and noninteger lengths. offset must be an integer from -1000000000 through 1000000000, excluding booleans; otherwise raise ValueError, even for empty bands.

The function must leave the caller's bands list and every contained record unchanged, both on a successful return and when raising ValueError. This includes ordinary nonempty calls whose result differs from the input.
